en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Cishou Shen By Han Ju,
Knight of the Second Class of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Hall of August Manners,
Supervisor of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, and Recipient of the Purple Golden Fish Bag. Introduction.

In ancient times, those who taught never failed to rely upon written characters. It was not until Bodhidharma of the Liang dynasty that he began to teach his disciples without establishing written texts.
Yet, by saying "not establishing [them]," he had already manifested the use of writing; how much more so for all other matters?
Since the time of Bodhidharma, those who served as teachers have often had their disciples privately record their teachings, which are known as *yulu* (recorded sayings).
Indeed, the Chan teachings currently circulating throughout the world amount to no fewer than tens of millions of words.

How, then, can it be said that they do not establish anything? If one knows that the nature of words is empty and that speech is fundamentally non-speech, then even tens of millions of words remain unestablished.
When the Elder Cishou first resided at Zifu, he later withdrew to a hermitage in the remote reaches of Mount Jiangshan. For many years...
In his later years, his reputation grew even more renowned. Consequently, he moved through six different monastic seats and thrice received the imperial summons of the Son of Heaven.
Wherever he went, scholars flocked to him. His lifelong exposition of the Dharma was complete and perfect.

If there were those capable of listening—like the forest trees and the water birds—then people could attain awakening and entry [into the truth]. His merit was no small matter. One should gradually seek it out...
Upon further reflection, it is not only the fault of those who preached the Dharma; those who compiled this narrative share in the responsibility.
On the first day of the eleventh month in the third year of the Xiangxing era.
Preface to the First Volume of the Extensive Record of Master Cishou Shen
Recorded Sayings of Zifuku Zen Temple;
Recorded Sayings of Jōzan Zen Temple;
Recorded Sayings of Eirin Zen Temple.

Verses of Praise;
Fascicle Three.
Preface to the Collection of Verses on Ancient Cases for Ascending the Dharma Hall at Huelin Chan Monastery,

Volume One of the Extensive Record of Master Cishou Shen.
Compiled by Attendant Śāṇakṣema, the Record of the Words of Master Cishou Shen at Zifu Monastery.
On the tenth day of the eighth month in the third year of the Zhenghe era, the Master accepted his invitation at Changlu. Holding up the formal document, he said:
Unable to bear the repeated hardships of these people, my meager fortune ultimately brings me much shame.
The morning apes and night cranes must surely laugh at me for stretching out my head into this noisy basket. He then conferred the certificate upon the *vina* (chant master).
The Master, receiving the Dharma robe from the hands of Master Zu Zhao, said: "After it was stored away at Mount Kukkutapada, clouds locked the thousand peaks; now it is divided at Caoxi."

Having been entrusted [to me], its sound has been transmitted through the ages. Were it not for descendants of the School’s lineage and children of the Patriarchs’ house, who would dare to take responsibility for this ground?
He then spread out his hands and said: "I do not seek extraordinary brilliance; I simply require that the color of the fur be distinct.
Having donned the Dharma robe, the Master looked toward the assembly and said: "If you wish to see the 'breaking of the half' and 'shattering of the three,' or to sing 'nine' as 'ten,' you must..."
"Facing toward the heights, let us meet with all people. The Master then ascended the seat and said: "The ancient mirror has long been buried in dust, resting in complacency;

its brilliance concealed and its radiance hidden, it has passed through the cold of the years. Today, within the treasury of light, nothing can be found; it hangs high in the empty hall for you to behold as you please.
Is there anyone who can distinguish the beautiful from the ugly? If so, please come forth and reflect upon it. A monk asked: "Master, now..."
[The monk] said, "I have already accepted the true invitation according to the ritual; how shall I proclaim the final phrase? The Master said, "A note.
The monk stepped forward and said, "A single word circulates universally; a thousand chariots share the same ruts. The Master said, "Few people travel the road to Caoxi.

The monk said, "One must know that clouds and waters cannot conceal it; dragons and spirits naturally push it forth. The Master said, "I, this old monk, do not know. A monk asked, "In the past, at Beichan..."

[The Master] said, "I request that you do not go. This morning, Zifu has already taken up the responsibility. [The student] asked, "Is this because there is ground for such causal conditions, or is it simply because of the timing?
The Master said, "Water flows downward; its squareness or roundness depends on the vessel. [The student] further asked, "When there is a deliberate mind at work, there is still error;
when there is no intention to seek, it is spontaneously so. The Master said, "Having a mind and having no mind—neither of these is it."
The Master then said: "Open the true eye of the crown of the head; it illuminates the past and the present. Emit the divine light from behind the nape; it is without interior or exterior.
If you are one of those within this circle, do not harbor attachments where there is illumination; remain ever solitary within that light. When questioned, be like the tips of arrows meeting;
when answering, be like glue and lacquer joining. Bring forth the tongs and hammer of the higher realm; draw out the gold."
A sword of adamantine jewel. At such a time as this, is there still any meeting? One does not see Zhaozhou saying: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell;
where there is no Buddha, run past quickly. Three thousand miles away, do not mistakenly raise [this matter] when meeting people."
Since it is thus, for what reason have you come here? Three thatched huts; with one request, he departed. After a long silence, he said:
"The sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice; the medicine comes out of the golden jar because of the illness."
The Master was at Changlu when he took leave of the assembly. A monk asked, "Master, you are now about to enter the red dust of the world; as you part ways at this crossroads, what is your intention?
The Master said, "Yellow leaves fall profusely at the head of the ancient road. The monk pressed further, "I am ashamed that my own nature is so full of resistance and compliance;
I cannot follow in the Master's footsteps. The Master said, "To put on these straw sandals is not yet late. The monk pressed further, "I specifically offer this one cry of 'returning home.'"
The flute: blown through the Mùluó River deep into the night. The Master said, "And so it goes again. The Master then said:
"One movement and one stillness, like wild cranes soaring; sometimes contracting and sometimes expanding, like drifting clouds gathering and dispersing."
There is no division between north and south; how could there be coming or going? The mind of a man of the Way is likewise so.
If it is thus, then even in the bustling marketplace of red dust, within tiger dens and demon palaces, he is present everywhere and finds benefit wherever he goes.

Amidst green waters and blue mountains, his refined sentiments are perfectly expressed; amidst red dock and white pondweed, his traveling countenance is suddenly illuminated. Now, please hoist your light sails high and set forth.
The short oars are frequently shaken; a single phrase at the parting of ways—how can one bear not to hold you in high esteem?
On the seventeenth day of the eighth month, the Master entered the monastery and returned directly to the Abbot’s quarters.

Taking his seat, he declared: "In years past, Mahākāśyapa alone closed the gate; silver mountains and iron walls cannot be scaled. Now the Great Gate of Generosity is opened; let Mara and Buddha both cease."

Having granted permission for his departure and return, he then struck the drum and ascended the seat. A monk asked, "Having bid farewell to the green reeds by the riverbank, you have now arrived at the White Sand Monastery.
What is the Immovable Honored One? The Master said, "He sits, cutting off everything at once. The monk stepped forward and said, "The wind blows and the grass bends.
The Master said, "Behold the decree being executed. The monk said, "Master of the House, you have appeared in the world too late. The Master—
He said, "The tea pitcher from Gong County. The Master then laughed heartily and said, "A few thatched huts cannot bear the worries;
for what purpose have you come to be the head of the kitchen? Fortunately, there is the bell from the beginning of the kalpa; whether poor or rich, one remains elegant in one's own way.
He then asked, "As for that bell from the beginning of the kalpa, how was it measured, and what sound did it produce? Thereupon, he struck the ground with his staff.
One day he said: "A single slight shake stirs heaven and earth.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Beating the drum to play with a monkey."

The student asked, "What is it like after seeing? The Master said, "The drum is broken and the monkey runs off. Later, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'the drum is broken and the monkey runs off'?
The Master said, "All cleverness comes to an end. The student said, "One does not gain a single bit of wisdom without encountering a particular matter.
The Master said, "You have not yet attained rest. The Master then said: "For those who have not yet entered the gate, during their time..."
There must be interaction. Yet for one who has already entered the gate, it is essential that there be no interaction.

For one who has already entered the gate to have interaction is like a tortoise bearing a map; it is a sign of its own impending destruction. For one who has not yet entered the gate, there is no interaction.
It is like abandoning one's father and fleeing, with no time of arrival at home in sight; yet there must be an encounter, while one actually requires no encounter.
Within this state of no encounter, there must nevertheless be an encounter. Even if you reach such a stage, that is precisely "coming out from within the gate";
you must know how to "go out through the body. Now tell me, what is the phrase for "going out through the body"?
The Way. Once, he was scolded with tears by a beautiful woman; to this day, he is ashamed to see chrysanthemums in the rain.
On the occasion of the Double Ninth Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "On this day each year is the Double Ninth; The chrysanthemums on the hedge seem to recall the fragrance of last year.
Do not laugh at how the branches are so withered and frail; From now on, there shall be a different way to deliberate. Do you understand? You have already attained the excellence of the True Man."
News. But tell me, what kind of news is this? The flavor of new rice and sesame cakes is excellent; how much more so when sugar is added to the place where they are eaten.
[The Master] ascends the hall, strikes the meditation staff once, and says: "A single move by Zifu—any attempt to deliberate upon it is an error. Only those with clear eyes are true monks."
"Self-binding without a rope. He then struck the table once and said, "Zifu has a single aperture—most profound, most wondrous.
If you can realize it directly, I will let you laugh in derision."
Ascending the hall, he said: "To have a question and an answer is to be entangled in elaboration; to be wordless and speechless is to fall into silence.
Even if a stubborn rock were to nod its head, how could it compare to returning to the hall to warm oneself by the fire?"
On account of the snow, he ascended the hall and said: "The white elephant in the pen has been lost; The old man of Emei laughs himself downwind.
The scholar on the street lacks refined discernment; All night long before his lamp, he composes poems on the snow. I, this poor monk, shall also give you a matching verse.
After a long silence, he said: "A bridge spans the silver rainbow; A stone lies like a jade qilin."
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "A single word of ultimate truth transforms the ordinary into the sacred. As a student has come before you, I pray that the Master will grant me an encounter.
The Master extended one foot. The monk said, "If a student were to depart in this very manner, what then? The Master withdrew his foot. The monk bowed and said, "The assembly has received your grace;
I, your student, offer my thanks. The Master then descended from the seat and returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Deshan showing the assembly: "Śākyamuni the Old Man is a stinking barbarian; Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are dung-carriers;
the two types of awakening, Equal and Wondrous, are hired laborers; the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas are tomb-keepers;
the entire Tripitaka is used paper for wiping impurities. Yunmen said: "To praise the Buddha and praise the Dharma, one must be..."
Deshan and Zifu are not like that. Deshan slanders the Buddha and slanders the Dharma; he has fallen to the bottom of the eighteen layers of hell.
With an iron yoke around his neck and his body lying upon an iron bed, he swallows iron pellets when hungry and drinks molten copper when thirsty. Why is this so?
It is simply because he lacks even a fraction of the Buddha-dharma within his mind and body. When Zifu speaks thus, is there still [anyone who understands]?
"Is it the Buddha-dharma, the body, or the mind? Now tell me: is it better to have a body and mind that possess the Buddha-dharma, or is it better to have no body and mind of the Buddha-dharma?
Do not treat idle talk as mere idle talk; often enough, matters arise from idle talk. I shall remain standing for a long while; take care."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring breeze sweeps away the snow before the courtyard; the warm sun hastens the blossoming of flowers upon the branches. Every thing, every state, reveals the truth.
Do not allow your mind-ground to become as chaotic as tangled hemp. Every person is a Buddha, yet sentient beings do not realize it in their daily activities.

Each one is perfectly complete, yet who understands how to turn the light back to reflect? It is simply because the arising of emotion creates a barrier to wisdom, and conceptual thought transforms the essence."
It is extraordinary that people cannot directly accept this; they often miss it right before their own eyes. For instance, a monk asked Fayan:
"Huishao asks the Master, 'What is the Buddha? Fayan said, 'You are Huishao. The Master remarked: "This conversation—"

One must be a man who can cut through things with a single stroke; only then will it be achieved. Were one to hesitate or engage in deliberation, there would immediately be thousands of mountains and ten thousand rivers.
Entering the hall, he said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like the three eyes of Maheśvara, and also like the three dots of the circle-ī."
With one eye, not even a hair’s breadth is attached; with one eye, the myriad phenomena are suddenly revealed; with one eye, the true and the conventional are merged as one.
For you practitioners of the patched robe, when you reach this point, you must further possess a distinct, authentic eye before you can succeed. Do you understand?
Those with copper heads and iron jaws cannot deliberate upon it.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year, he said: "Patch-robed monks need not look at others' lamps; they possess their own single bright lamp from of old.
With tattered robes covering their heads, they sit facing the wall; the numinous light pierces through the Iron Encircling Mountains."

Ascending the hall, he said: "The cycle of ten thousand kalpas of saṃsāra exists because of deluded thoughts; as soon as the single mind ceases, birth and death are at rest. Buddhas and demons are but idle furniture;
casting off one's hands over the precipice, one attains freedom. But tell me, how do you express this word of freedom?
'Since childhood I have observed the fast until now I am old; seeing people, I lack the strength to descend from my meditation seat.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "If there were even a single dharma, Vairocana would fall into the rank of ordinary beings. If the myriad dharmas were non-existent, Samantabhadra would lose his realm.
If one attains the state where both existence and non-existence are exhausted, ordinary and sagely beings are merged as one; thus, Nanquan need not invoke 'suchness'."
Zhaozhou does not reside within clarity. He is like a great furnace with fierce flames—how could he distinguish between hairpins, bracelets, vases, or basins?
He is like a bright mirror set upon its stand—do not ask about blue, yellow, red, or white. At such a time as this, tell me: is there illumination, or is there function?
"How do you explain the phrase 'capable of killing and capable of reviving'? After a long silence, he said: "The walls have ears. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Studying the Way and applying effort is just like a person digging a well. One day they see the spring source; throughout their life, it will never be exhausted. He then asked:
"How do you explain the phrase 'never-ending enjoyment'? A single drop universally moistens the sands."
The realms are moistened; throughout the ten directions, the sound of the pulley has ceased.
Entering the hall, he said: "In the springtime of the second month, the weather is pleasantly clear for the first time. The swallows speak from the carved beams with such fine voices.
If you can understand the meaning of Xuansha on that day, you will be able to strike the third watch at midday. He struck his staff once and said, "Vibrant and agile!"
Deshan was exceptionally sharp-witted; when he looked at him, Deshan’s hair stood on end with cold. "There is no need to go to the Southern Mountain to seek the Turtle-Nose.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What kind of person is not swallowed by impermanence? The Master said, "I only fear that he has no place to put his mouth.
The monk said, "If so, then a single thought penetrates the profound arrow, and the three *śava* demons lose their guile. The Master said, "You..."
"There is one thought; it will certainly be swallowed by another. The monk asked, "What is it when there is not even a single thought?
The Master said, "I have caught you, O *śāli*! The Master then said: "Bubbles arise and bubbles perish thousands of times, solely because the diamond eye (*vajranetra*) does not open.
One day, when the waves of the river of craving subside, one will finally know that there is neither going nor coming. You all—waves!"
Has the wave subsided? Has the Vajra Eye opened? If this eye opens, it illuminates all phenomena as being like dreams and illusions;

one should know that this body is like a shadow and like an echo. Severs the path of the thousand sages in a single sitting, falling neither into the stages of the patriarchs nor into the ranks of the Buddhas.
There is neither person nor Buddha. The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble in the ocean; all sages and worthies—
"Like a flash of lightning sweeping by. Tsk!
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites Master Xuansha, who pointed to a lantern and asked a monk, 'I call this a lantern;
what do you call it? The monk said, 'I also call it a lantern. Xuansha said, 'Throughout the entire land of the Great Tang...'"
"Not a single person has ever realized the Buddha-dharma. The Master said, "They do not know. What would a person who has realized the Buddha-dharma call a lantern?
He ascended the hall and cited Chan Master Dahui Huanyuan’s address to the assembly, which said: "I, this old monk, cannot answer questions; I simply..."
When Daci recognized the illness, a monk came forth, and he immediately returned to his quarters. The Master said, "Daci has indeed correctly diagnosed the illness, yet he lacks the medicine.
He then ascended the hall and cited the case where Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "Where does one who knows 'there is' go? Nanquan replied, "He goes to..."
Shanxia said, "I am going to become a water buffalo. Zhou said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master.
Quan said, "Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window. The Master said, "Nanquan shakes his head; Zhaozhou wags his tail. Look closely, and both have lost ground."
Rising from illness, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "In the past, when Vimalakīrti was ill, it was for the sake of all sentient beings.
Today, when the Master is unwell, for what purpose is it? The Master said, "Today I have encountered someone to scrutinize me. The monk said, "The Master has an illness."
Everyone knew this. When someone among the assembly fell ill, [the monk] asked, "How can he be healed? The Master said, "Ācārya, you should drink ginger-and-attachment soup.
The monk said, "A sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; medicine comes from the golden jar because it is applied to an illness.

The Master said, "Tell me, how far apart are the illness of the Buddha and the illness of the Patriarchs? The monk said, "One stroke across them both. The Master said, "In the midst of the blue sky..."

Adding further to his grievous suffering, the Master said: "His illness has cleared, yet his crane-like bones are emaciated and jagged; he is utterly unable to speak of the wondrous or discuss the profound.
Fortunately there is his companion, Elder Wood, who is robust and more alert than ever. Thereupon, he took up his staff.
He struck the meditation desk once and said, "Since you are so alert, I ask that you preach some Zen for the assembly. He then cast down his staff and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Ascending the hall for the conclusion of the summer retreat, he said: "In the monasteries throughout the world today, the summer session has ended.
How many monks will now redouble their spirit? Since the mouth of the sack has been opened, each must provide his own straw sandals.

At the place where there is not a blade of grass ten thousand miles away, realize the house style of Dongshan. To receive thirty blows out of sheer necessity, you must grasp the pivot of Yunmen. And so it is.
"The Way relies upon the intention of merit. Where does it reside? After a long silence, he said: "When meeting people, do not speak erroneously.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked: "Yunmen said: 'I do not ask about the period before the fifteenth day; what about the period after the fifteenth day?'"
"Bring me a phrase of the Way. "I do not know what the meaning of the ancient’s intent was. The Master said, "Today is the seventeenth.
The monk said, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. The Master said, "Believe half of it for now. The monk said, "What about after the fifteenth day?
The Master said, "Go and look where the body has divided into two places. The monk said, "In that case, people come from Chenzhou..."
"Come! But you are heading off toward Xuzhou. The Master said, "What do you know of good and evil?
The Master then continued: "The ancients were too poor; people today are too rich. Only Old Man Cishou’s household style is not like that:
when there is oil, he lights a lamp; when there is charcoal, he sits by the fire. When there is neither oil nor charcoal, everyone sits together in the dark until their bones ache."
His buttocks were in pain. He lay down with both legs fully extended; at dawn he rose to eat porridge. What need is there to speak of meeting Bodhidharma while lost?

When the Master arrived at Changlu, the assembly requested him to ascend the seat. A monk asked, "Upon the banks of the Ten Rivers, within the field of the ancient Buddhas, when these two elders meet, what matters should they discuss?
The Master said, "Six ears do not share a secret. The monk stepped forward and said, "Auspicious mists arise from the seat."

Auspicious vapors arose in the courtyard. The Master said, "Better that good things do not exist. The student advanced and said, "It can be said that after one who knows the music is known, who else could know it?
Why need the pure breeze move heaven and earth? The Master said, "Only you, O *dārala*, remain unrecognized.
The student said, "From the beginning, my nostrils reach the heavens; I will not accept being drenched by another. The Master said, "Torn apart! The student said, "For a long time..."
Hearing that Zifu possessed such a vital pivot, the Master said, "A groundless cause for sorrow. The student stepped forward and said, "The assembly bears witness;
this student bows in thanks. The Master then said: "The Way has never been subject to interruption; Do not distinguish between city and forest springs.
Returning again to the place where you seek the Dharma, The pure breeze remains as it was before, filling the space before your eyes. Truly, one knows that the Dharma is without..."
It is certainly also to follow conditions: when in the mountain forests, not a single worldly task is performed; when entering the realm of dust and toil, ten thousand functions are all swept away.
Whether moving or still, there is nothing that is not within the realm of true purity; whether going or coming, it is entirely within the field of Bodhi.
It is like a fist becoming a palm—the opening and closing occur at their proper times; it is like water producing waves—their arising and ceasing have no fixed point. Therefore, for long...
The reeds sing the Yunmen melody; Zifu joins in with the Deshan song. Every beat is impartial; every point has its basis.
There is no further talk of the mysterious or the subtle, nor any suppressing of the past to exalt the present. Naturally, water and milk blend together;
there is no need to ask whether streams and mountains differ. Even so, should there suddenly be someone whose spirit is not at peace who comes forward, let them shout out at the top of their voice!

He said, "Not understanding, you cause a disturbance in the forest. Furthermore, how would you have Zifu respond? After a long silence, he said, "In the end, it would have been better to let the prisoner remain in custody rather than increase his wisdom."
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice, he said: "Today, the Yang energy begins to rise; tomorrow, we shall count the nine days. Zhang San remains as fat as ever; Li Si has always been thin.
Having consumed every medicine under heaven, the old ailment remains as it was before. Having exhausted one's own mind, [the original condition persists]."
It breaks the mouths of others with laughter. Why is this so? The flower’s root is originally brilliant; the tiger’s body is inherently striped. Entering the hall, he said:
"Last night, a great snow overturned the void; the jade palace and silver towers were pure and bright.
When dawn comes and no one is in the courtyard, do not say the mountain monk does not speak. Even so, it still deceives and kills people."
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "The east wind has blown away the clouds of the dawn sky; The great earth, mountains, and rivers have all turned to spring.
There is no need to write 'Great Auspiciousness' upon the gate; Within this, there are neither ghosts nor gods."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: A monk asked Yunmen, “What is it like when the rain has lasted long and does not stop?
Yunmen said, “Zip! Someone asked Zifu, “What is it like when the rain has lasted long and does not stop? This mountain monk answered him simply, “Gather up.
Yunmen’s “Zip” and Zifu’s “Gather up”—one seizing, one releasing—each has its own reason. Last night the spring wind blew through the tips of the trees; at dawn, the blossoms were red.
The sun rises above the clouds; I laugh at Master Pudu of the Twin Trees for saying instead that "the bridge flows, but the water does not flow.
On the occasion of the Yuanxiao Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Last night the lamps and candles vied in brilliance; how many sentient beings were busy until dawn!"

In the end, they do not realize that the lamp is fire; they have obscured the single point of light within the spirit-mansion (*lingtai*). Is there anyone who can turn the light back upon themselves to reflect?
Return to the hall and drink some tea.
Ascending the hall, he said: "This morning we ate congee too late. Xu Liu at the street corner carries a single board;
he knows only to beat the drum and ascend the hall, unaware that it is already time for a meal again. After eating congee, one eats rice; after eating rice, one eats congee.
Under the clear breeze and moonlight, the man who waits by the stump finds the cool rabbit gradually receding as the spring grass turns green."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Zen Master Yunju Qi asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the hall.
Qi said, "How can you speak falsely? The monk was speechless. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "This monk committed a minor falsehood;
Yunju committed a major falsehood."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Luzu. Whenever a monk came to see him, Luzu would simply face the wall. Liangshan had a verse that said: "Luzu’s samādhi is the most effortless:
As soon as he sees a monk coming, he faces the wall. If one is a person who understands the pivot and masters the Way, Their mind will naturally come to rest right then and there.
A monk then requested further instruction from Langya Guangzhao. Guangzhao said: "The Patriarch facing the wall spread [this teaching]..."
"In all directions, many monks vainly attempt to measure this. It is best to gaze upon the river at dusk; a few branches of cold cypress lean against the setting sun. The Master said:
"Zifu does not use yellow or black ink to criticize the ancients; he simply wishes for everyone to know that there is something here.
Luzu’s wall-gazing was a state of exhausted words and meager principle. Guangzhao and Liangshan were like those who fear snakes before they even see them. If you ask Cishou, he would split—"
Ji spoke thus and struck [the gong].
Chan Master Fojian retired from Zhihai and went to Zifuku. The Master ascended the hall and said: "We once met beneath Mount Taiping;
clapping my hands, I laughed with an open face. Do not wonder that my good reputation has spread to ten thousand mouths; it is only when leaning on my staff that I am truly myself."

[The Master] came from the edge [of the assembly]. After descending from his seat, he bowed and requested the Zen Master to speak a few words for the sake of the fourfold assembly regarding the "Talks of the Eastern Capital.

On the morning of the following day, he ascended the hall and said: "The Golden Wheel governs the world, and heaven and earth endure forever; When the Jade Candle is tuned, the universe shines bright. The peach..."
Li Wuyan, the spring is in full bloom; I know not how to repay this era of peace and prosperity.
Entering the hall, he raised the following case: When Zhaozhou was sitting, an attendant reported, "The Great King is coming! Zhaozhou descended from his rope seat and said: [“...”]
"Great King, ten thousand blessings! The attendant said, "Not yet. Zhaozhou said, "And yet you say he has come.
The Master said, "It is all the same 'radish-head' Chan; once it falls into Zhaozhou's hands, it possesses an unfailing fine flavor."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is existence is not existence. He struck the meditation seat several times and asked, "Can it be called non-existence?
"Where there is non-existence is not non-existence. Holding up his whisk, he said, "Can it be called existence? "Neither existence nor non-existence is the place;
the traces of Buddhas and Patriarchs are submerged, yet their fragrance fills the paths. Everywhere, they fill the ditches and block the ravines. You men of clear eyes, try to examine this!"
Look! [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "I cite the case where Lord Lu asked Nanquan: 'In my home, I have been raising a gosling in a jar.
Lately it has grown quite large. I wish to take this gosling out, yet I cannot break the jar, nor can I harm the gosling.'"
"I do not yet understand, Master. Nanquan said, "There is a skillful means. He called out, "Attendant Lu! The Attendant responded, "Yes?
Nanquan said, "It has already come out. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Nanquan’s nostrils were already in Attendant Lu’s hands.
At that time, had he seen him ask such a question, he should have simply said to him, "In your belly, you have all these calculations. He also said, "The Buddha-dharma is not..."

Regarding this principle, he ascended the hall and said, citing Baizhang Huaihai: "Since my youth, I have herded a single water buffalo. If I intend to let it loose on the east bank of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king’s water and grass;
if I intend to let it loose on the west bank of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king’s water and grass."
"It is better to accept a little according to one's lot. The Master said, "The Abbot of Mt. Gui was much like a rustic elder who did not recognize the labors of Yao and Shun;
he spent his remaining life plowing fields and digging wells. Little did he know that within the sphere of every person, there is a water buffalo to be herded."
That which you tread upon throughout the twelve periods of the day is the King’s field; that which you drink and eat is the King’s water and grass.
From of old, its horns have been towering and majestic, let alone the fact that its coat is of a different hue. Do you all recognize it yet?
If you do recognize it, there is no kindness that will not be repaid and no Dharma that will not be penetrated. If this is not yet so, then do not distinguish between east, west, south, and north.
"Separate! All is contained within the single transformation of our Emperor.

He ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'Patience, patience—the grudges of three lifetimes are exhausted from this point on. Forgiveness, forgiveness—the myriad calamities and thousand misfortunes vanish from this point on.
Silence, silence—unsurpassed Bodhi emerges from this point on. The Master said: 'If you can understand these three kinds [of teachings]...'"
Understood. What an unpleasant fellow! This mountain monk simply takes a bull from one person and returns a horse to another;
he splashes water on them and spits at them, thrusting his snout in and cursing them back. (He strikes the meditation staff once. "Out! Out!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The flow of true permanence has turned tens of thousands of times; empty space neither goes nor comes.
Within this, where is there room for birth and death? Smash the mirror-stand right here in the hall!"

Ascending the hall, he said: "In the sky, wild geese fly in formation, seven or eight points; at the sea gate, the sun rises two or three poles high. The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is clearly present;
it is simply that people of this age do not know how to look at it. Even if you were able to see it, it would still be like trying to fit a square peg into a round hole."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: At midnight, Zihu was in the monks' hall, shouting, "Catch the thief!
Catch the thief! The assembly of monks started up in alarm. One monk was seized by Zihu, who said, "I have him! I have him! The monk cried out repeatedly, "It is not I!"
"I. Hu said, "That is indeed so; it is simply that you are unwilling to accept it. The Master said, "Zihu was merely pressing the ox's head down to make it eat grass."
Ascending the hall, he said: "When the mind and its objects are suddenly dissolved, only then does one clearly understand form and emptiness.

If you wish to recognize the original substance, look amidst the green mountains and white clouds. The Master said: "When National Teacher Longji spoke thus, he was casting sand and scattering earth into the eyes of future generations;
until this very day, they have failed to distinguish black from yellow. Today, for your sakes, I shall use a golden probe to scrape away the film."
Adjusting his two eyes, he causes each and every one of them to open a single eye at the crown of their heads.

When mind and境 (objects) are suddenly dissolved, only then will color and emptiness be clearly understood. Wishing to recognize the original substance, he then held up his whisk and, after a long silence, said:
"Sailing a boat upon a mountain while riding the wind upon the sea."

Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Yunmen, who said: "There are three kinds of people: one attains enlightenment because of an explanation; one attains enlightenment because of being called by name;
and one turns back immediately upon hearing the case cited. Now tell me, what is the meaning of turning back immediately upon hearing the case cited?"
"I would give him thirty blows. The Master said, "Yunmen was much like letting out a hawk upon seeing a rabbit.
On a day of heavy snow, he ascended the hall and said: "In the four quarters and above and below, all is a vast whiteness; the jade palace and crystal towers are most fair to behold.
Even if black winds blow and the sea stands up, they have no concern with his gate. On the road to Caoxi, there are no tracks and no footprints.
At the foot of the Shaoshi Rock, dripping water freezes; the fan of Yanguan is set aside;
Zhaozhou’s cloth robe has not a trace of warmth. At such a time as this, what is the phrase that is impervious to cold and heat?
The stone woman knows how to plant a tree without shadow; the wooden man can sow lotuses in the midst of fire.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said: "The people of this age all bow in greeting the year; I, a mountain monk, do not celebrate the New Year.
The early spring is still cold; how often have the sun and moon shifted? After this day last year, it is before this day this year. That which is new and old is not the same."
"Who comes after and who comes before? The Master said, "The great masters Longji and Shanju were hindered by this 'old year' and 'new year.
Though they could expound so many principles, in the end they could not avoid smearing their lips and staining their teeth. Compassionate Receptor (Cishou Sou) was not like this:
when the people all bowed for the New Year, the mountain monk also offered his greetings. A single point of radiance remains; listen from the two wheels."

He moved on. Conforming to worldly custom, he raised his hands in the *añjali* gesture; harmonizing with the light, he spoke briefly of Chan. "If you can understand this point," he said, "the Buddhas and Patriarchs originally have no transmission.

Leaving the monastery and bidding farewell to the assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "For three years I have dwelt here amidst the appearance of empty flowers; today I return to the moon reflected in water."

The same. Whether going or staying, there is no need to distinguish between self and other. In human life, all things turn to emptiness in the blink of an eye. Practice the myriad practices as empty flowers;
sit in meditation within a water-moon dharma-hall; subdue the demon armies within a mirror; and accomplish the Buddha-work within a dream. Thus we know:
the Buddhas of the three periods speak of dreams; the six generations of patriarchs speak of dreams; and the elder monks of the world speak of dreams.
This morning at Zifu, I spoke of a dream. I have spoken of this one dream for three years and seven months.
During that time, those of sharp faculties merely had their names called out lightly and immediately turned their heads; yet those of duller natures remain in the dream even now.
I, this mountain monk, have a phrase for startling those who are dozing off; as I depart, I cannot help but pour out my heart and empty my belly. It is all finished.
I have sent this as a message for your benefit. Be careful of your nostrils; it seems you have strayed somewhat far.
I pray you take care of yourself. Compiled by the attendant Shansui, from the *Recorded Sayings of Venerable Cishou Shen* at Jiaoshan.
On the sixth day of the ninth month in the seventh year of the Zhenghe era, the Master accepted an invitation at Mount Jiangshan.
Holding up the imperial edict, he said: "The imperial decree from the heavens above summons the slumbering man of West Hermitage. Whether it be an auspicious omen or a lucky sign, let no one inquire;
he is a golden-maned lion and a jade qilin. If you understand it thus, even the mountain forests will flourish with beauty."
"Qi! The springs and rocks possess eternal clarity. Should this not yet be so, I request the Rector to proclaim it once more with a loud voice.

Having finished proclaiming the edict, the Master ascended the seat. A monk asked: "To avoid clamor and seek stillness, there has never been a method for dwelling in the world; you have now raised the West Hermitage again."
"What is the one phrase for benefiting others? The Master said, "The divine blade leaning against the sky; its light chills those who behold it.

The student asked, "If that is so, then the green mountains cannot conceal it, yet the bright moon allows it to be seen. The Master said, "How many people truly know their own minds? The student asked again.
"Good wine is not found in deep alleys; pungent vinegar is enough for anyone to buy.

The Master said, "You fellows who eat only dregs of wine! The Master then continued, "The Dharma has no stagnation; coming and going, its fundamental substance is always as it is. The Way also follows conditions;

how could there ever be a gap between the streams and mountains? You must know that in abiding, there is no abiding, yet one abides; in walking, there is no walking, yet one walks. He opened [the teaching].
At the gate, the direction of joy is cold and whistling; on level ground, suddenly there is a tumultuous clamor. Like a fist becoming an open palm, opening and closing occur at their own time;
like waves arising from water, movement and stillness have no fixed state. Now tell me: who is it that does not involve itself in coming and going?
The moon travels beyond the clouds, shining without intent; the water reaches the human realm, spontaneously perfecting itself.
At Jiangshan, before departing for the assembly, he ascended the hall. A monk asked: "Having left Mount Zhongfu and not yet reached Mount Jiaofeng, how do you avoid the two extremes?"
"Please, Master, speak quickly. The Master said, "A single wild goose flies across the autumn sky; at night, a thousand households have their mortars and pestles sounding.

The student advanced and said, "Auspicious vapors arise by the Iron Cauldron City; atop the peaks of Haimen, heavy clouds are locked fast. The Master said, "In the future, at Jiaoshan, I shall give you a cup of tea to drink.
The student said, "May the assembly bear witness. This student bows in gratitude. The Master said, "We are both without any expedient means."
The Master then said: "Joyfully having found the stratagem, I close the deep pass; my mouth is parched and my heart ashen, all in a state of singular leisure.
I laugh at myself for being without any choice in my conduct and concealment, yet again following karmic conditions as I pass beyond Mount Jiao."
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Master entered the monastery and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. Taking his seat, he said: "This single room is vast and empty;

what thing is here? The Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones vie with one another to inquire. If a patch-robed monk does not understand the phrase before the wind, Any attempt to deliberate will fall short by two or three."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was the intent of the ancients when they sat facing a wall? The Master said, "The mouth is the gateway to calamity.
The monk pressed further, "How many matters in the world are entirely contained within silence? The Master said, "Your nostrils are already in my hands.
The monk pressed further, "I have long heard that the Master’s commands are strict. The Master said, "The hand that casts the line merely toils idly while sitting on the fishing platform."
The Master then said: "White artemisia and red smartweed by the riverbank in autumn; short oars and light sails, moving with freedom.
To understand the single phrase of 'arriving home,' the long river flows eastward as it has always done."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Carrying water to sell at the riverhead. The monk followed up, "Is there anything further beyond the Buddha?
The Master said, "A person of keen intelligence is hard to find. The Master then said, "The twentieth day of the eleventh month."
They call it the Great Winter Solstice. Zhang San congratulates Zheng Po; Li Si bows to Wang Qi. From dawn until night, they exhaust all their lifelong strength.
Yet only those of the patched-robed monastic family do not strike these drums and pipes. Why is this so?
An iron-faced child from Kunlun—his entire body is black as lacquer.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is the samādhi of non-contention? The Master took up his staff, stepped down from the seat, and struck the monk three times.
The monk cried out, "What fault have I committed? The Master set down his staff and said, "You should have spoken sooner.
He then returned to the abbot’s quarters.
On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and said: "When Gautama studied the Way, he sat beneath the Bodhi tree.
Suddenly, upon seeing the morning star, his lacquer bucket was shattered. Only when it was shattered did he finally believe that the lamp from of old was indeed fire.

People today who study the Way do not awaken to it; they pursue it through the paths of logic and seek it externally. To further claim that there has never been awakening or delusion is very much like a mere circle."
[He] swallowed a jujube.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "When one knows it exists but cannot speak of it, what then? The Master said, "A mute man eating honey. The monk pressed further.
"You have spoken the Way. But do you know how it is at times? The Master said, "A parrot calls out to people. The monk bowed.

The Master said, "This fellow who merely transmits words. The Master then said: "Today is the Dragon Boat Festival. To express our gratitude to the neighbors, we must bring forth the seasonal occasion.
Do not ask about the hundred cords wrapped around one's wrists; for now, let us eat the *zongzi* with sugar. Tell me, where does the flavor lie?"
In what place? Cold things should also be eaten sparingly.

He ascended the hall and said: "If it is a pillar, you do not see the pillar; if it is not a pillar, you do not see the pillar. Once 'is' and 'is not' have been eliminated, there is still a distance of three hundred paces remaining."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up Xuefeng’s statement: “If you recognize this staff, the business of a lifetime of study is finished.
Hearing this, Luoshan said, “If you recognize this staff, buy another pair of straw sandals and go on pilgrimage.
The Master said, “If you recognize this staff, it is so; it is not so, and it is also so.”
Ascending the hall, he raised an old case: A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is the realm of Jia Shan? Shan replied, "A monkey carries its young back behind the green peaks;
a bird picks up a flower before the azure cliffs. Fa Yan said, "For twenty years, I have understood this only as a description of a landscape."
The Master asked, "Do you understand? When thorns are planted at the gate, there are many pricks that tear through the infinite robes of one's descendants.
He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "A jade hare hidden within the clouds. The monk stepped forward and asked further.
"How is it after leaving the world? The Master said, "In the day, he releases the golden crow. The Master then said: "Five times five is twenty-five;
one phrase transcends past and present. Last night at Shigong Mountain, there was a place of joy. Do you all know it yet?"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When all seeking is suffering, what then? The Master said, "It is simply because one does not know contentment.
The monk pressed further, "After knowing contentment, what then? The Master said, "One no longer perceives suffering. The Master then said: "In receiving words, you must understand the source."
Do not establish your own rules and regulations; Master Shi’s mountain has already entered your nostrils. Do you know this?
If you say you know, it will block and suffocate you. If you say you do not know, the lanterns and pillars will deceive you.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “How does one realize the place where neither Buddha nor Mara reach? The Master said, “What do you say? The monk stepped forward and said, “In that case, all traces of activity are cut off.
The Master said, “Stretching out his hand, he meets no one. The Master then said, “Every word from Jiaoshan is medicine;
it is intended only for the peace and happiness of people of this time. Though one may exhaustively use croton seeds and arsenic, it only results in further complications.”

"Scattered and in disarray. For everyone, every step is illness; all day long their heads spin and their eyes whirl, doing nothing but using fire to fight fire, without understanding how to set the head straight and the tail straight.

Suddenly, there is a man who comes forward and says, 'Master, for you to speak thus is like having licorice on your tongue and yellow bitter gourd in your belly. The Master laughs heartily and says, 'There is something to it.'"
A letter from Chan Master Fojian of Jiangshan arrived. He ascended the hall and a monk asked: "The Dharma-boat has sunk and the Dharma-banner has collapsed;
boundless winds of sorrow come sweeping across the earth. We do not know where on Mount Zhong he has gone; we pray that the Master will thunder out a great roar."
The Master said, "Even an insentient staff frowns. The student advanced and said, "It cannot be detained within the ranks of Buddhas and Patriarchs;
it roams freely through the human world and the heavens. The Master said, "Can you still call out for a response? The student said, "From ancient times to the present, it has never fallen."
"It is clearly right before one's eyes. The Master said, "One coffin, two dead men. The student asked, "I too wish to join in the mourning today.
The Master said, "The eyes of a clay figure are red. The Master then said: "The spirit of the Chan school has long been desolate;
atop Mount Fojian, it has perished once more. Last night by the lamp, I counted on my fingers; I know not who can understand this."

To rectify the collapsing threads of discipline—at such a time, this Dharma gate has met with misfortune. On the eighth day of this month, Chan Master Fojian of Jiangshan suddenly passed away while sitting in meditation.
When the news of his death arrived, the initial inquiry left those who heard it breathless with sorrow.
Yet for a monk of our tradition, birth is like putting on a garment, and death is likewise like taking off one’s trousers; what cause, then, is there for lamentation? As for the Buddha—
In these times when the Dharma has grown thin and the administrative order lies prostrate on the ground, success depends upon finding the right person; failure comes with losing them.
Gazing westward toward the sacred shrine, I cannot overcome my grief and longing. The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Do you understand? Alas for the old water-buffalo of Zhongshan!
Whether going or staying, he acts with total freedom and no fixed constraints. For twenty years he has pulled out wedges and extracted nails, chewing through raw ginger until it is gone."
Having finished drinking the vinegar, sometimes one is poor, sometimes one is rich. Who understands the Southern Mountain dog biting a tiger?
The monks are as numerous as hemp seeds; who among them knows how to swallow the "Páng" phrase? Listen to Jiaoshan’s further pointing and commentary:
If you say Mount Zhong has a phrase, it is much like a vine leaning against a tree. If you say Mount Zhong has no phrase, that is precisely burying the Buddha.
The Patriarch said, "Tell me, after all, how is it? He then covered his face with his hand and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again.
A monk asked, "From what do the four elements and five aggregates arise? The Master said, "Where the spring breeze has just passed, the pond water naturally forms ripples.
The monk pressed further, "What is it like when one attains total stillness? The Master did not answer. The monk continued, "But this is precisely it!"
The student stirred up waves where there was no wind. The Master did not respond. The monk let out a long sigh, and the Master struck him.
The Master then said: "The river moon shines; the pine wind blows. Through the eternal night and clear sky, what is there to do?
If you are a guest from under Caoxi’s gate, there is no need to raise an eyebrow upon meeting."
When the Elder Lingyan retired from his seat and arrived at the mountain, the Master ascended the hall and said: "For what purpose has this small boat crossed the river?
Meeting beneath the forest trees, smiling faces unfold. There is no need to discuss salt and rice again; One must simply raise wind and thunder upon the tongue."
I have heard the name of Master Lingyan for many days, yet there has been no way to meet him face-to-face. What brings you here on your small boat to visit me so unexpectedly?

It can truly be said that meeting someone in person is superior to merely hearing their name; even better than meeting them, it is to see them as they are. Clapping my hands before the wind, I laugh heartily:
when viewed from this perspective, all things are but playthings. Thus one knows that empty space is devoid of self, freely manifesting its brilliance through both light and darkness.
Flowing water is originally tranquil; it moves freely according to the square and the round. This is why the Old Master Wang did not beat that drum or blow that flute—how much more convenient!
Chen Muzhou sat coldly in an empty room, yet he was nonetheless capable of discerning stillness.
Only after passing through such afflictions can one know that the ancients wandered aimlessly through the world because, fundamentally, they sought to clarify this very matter. Have you not seen?
Master Zhuxi visited Linji. As soon as Linji saw him, he gave a shout. Zhuxi said, "A double case. Linji said, "You wild fox spirit!
Zhuxi stepped forward, held up his sitting mat, and asked, "Is it when it is spread out, or is it when it is not spread out?
Linji shouted again. Zhuxi folded up his sitting mat and departed. Linji called out, "Thief! Thief! Zhuxi then went out. Do not say there was nothing happening.
"Good. Linji turned his head and asked the Head Seat, "In our meeting just now, was there anything gained or lost?
The Head Seat said, "There was. Linji said, "Did the guest lose or did the host lose? The Head Seat said, "Both lost. Linji said, "In what way did they lose?
The Head Seat shook his sleeves and walked away. Linji said, "Do not say that nothing happened. Later, a monk brought this up to Nanquan. (The story is not yet finished.)
"Examine the intentions of these three men. Quan said, "It is very much like official horses trampling one another. The Master said, "In the monastic groves, everyone deliberates on this, saying:
'Linji held the spiritual blade in his sleeve and did not need to command it; Zhuxi raised the rhombus-mirror in his palm and needed no intention to reflect things.
This is a lion in a lion’s den. Head Seat, you must investigate the beginning and end of this matter if you wish to know."
"The Bianliang Jade is flawless; it must have been Master Nanquan. Although this is so, if one examines it closely, it cannot be said that they were each without their own point of failure.
But tell me, where exactly was the point of failure? [The master] descends from the seat and requests Master Lingyan to provide a critical analysis for everyone.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: The Sixth Patriarch asked a monk, "Where have you come from?

The monk replied, "I previously attended upon Master Wo-lun and received a verse from him that I shall enjoy for the rest of my life. The Patriarch said, "Recite it for me. Wo-lun has skill; He can cut off a hundred thoughts.
When facing objects, his mind does not stir; Bodhi simply grows. The Patriarch then spoke this verse: 慧 (Huì) [The name of the monk who recited the verse].
"Being without skillful means, one does not sever the hundred thoughts; when the mind arises in response to objects, how can Bodhi grow? The Master said:
"These two old fellows are much like a clay man rubbing the back of a vajra-man.
Why? Jiaoshan has another verse: 'Existence and non-existence are both skillful means; they are all but human delusions. When the Magistrate strikes the laborer, he makes everyone laugh."
The Korean Official. The Lay Patron (Dānapati) views the Tripitaka; the Master ascends the hall. A monk asks: "How is it before the Treasure Store has been opened?
The Master says: "Who dares to add explanatory notes? The monk steps forward and says: "For forty-nine years it could not be spoken of; today at last my Master’s function is revealed. The Master—
[The Master] said, "There is a thorn in the soft mud. Jin asked, "What is it like after unrolling the scroll? The Master said, "That which Yaoshan spoke from the bottom of his heart.
Jin said, "Pointing to heaven and pointing to earth—do not deceive me. To cut through iron, one must rely on a person of true capacity.
The Master said, "Where you are struck and bumped, how will you evade it? Jin said, "When a student reaches this point, they can do nothing but receive it with faith and put it into practice."
The Master said, "I thought you were a master craftsman. The Master then said, "From the mind of great compassion, the Buddha brought forth the twelve divisions of the scriptures.
Their jade-bound volumes and precious cases fill as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges. Every word is a wondrous medicine; every character transcends past and present.
They are like the udumbara flower, difficult to encounter even in a hundred kalpas; they are also like a great bright lamp, capable of shattering [the darkness]."
In the place of darkness, it is like the power of wisdom that can sever the tree of ignorance; it is like a pearl necklace that can make a person wealthy.
The people of this vast, dusty world run about in haste like hares; they do not realize that old age has arrived, nor have they ever opened their eyes to look.
Only the Official Hua possesses a remarkably firm faith and devotion; he has charged me, a man of no-mind, to transmit this.
The words of all Buddhas: A floating life of a hundred years is just like dew upon a blade of grass. When one goes to bed, one’s shoes are left behind;
one cannot guarantee the morning, let alone the evening. Eat a little meat and burn a little more incense. The three vehicles—the sheep, the deer, and the ox—all travel this very path.
Then, raising his whisk, he said: "If you can understand it here, you may then believe, accept, and practice it. Its...
Perhaps not. Each of you should pay your respects and depart.
[The Master] ascends the hall. A monk asks: "The meal is late and we have yet to hear the tolling of the bells and drums; does the celebratory praise involve some other deliberation?"
The Master said, "Willingly he takes the golden needle to deliver it to others. The monk stepped forward and said, "The true meaning of Deshan lies entirely within his silence.
The Master said, "He is a toothless tiger; you are a yellow-tailed dog.
The monk bowed and asked, "What kind of mind-set do you have, Preceptor? The Master said, "I spare you no little. The Master then said, "A crane."
The traces of drifting clouds have no fixed dwelling. It has been more than half a year since our parting at White Sands. We meet again beneath the foot of Mount Jiao;
do you remember what happened back then? If you remember what happened back then, you will understand what is happening now.

If you understand what is happening now, you will finally know that throughout the twelve hours of the day—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, whether picking up the spoon or grasping the chopsticks—you have never failed to [act with mindfulness].
Meeting with a mountain monk, if the boundaries have not yet been distinguished, each meeting brings one closer to old age;
realize that this body is but a flower in the sky, a dream within a dream.
[The Master] ascends the hall to see off the Head of the Monastery. He cites Baizhang, who said: "You all shall work for me in clearing the fields; when you return, I will speak to you."
"Great Meaning. The monk said, "Why must you wait until I have returned? I request it right now. Baizhang extended both hands.
The Master said, "Baizhang speaking of 'Great Meaning' in this way has failed that monk. Today, I shall clearly explain it for you: Jiaoshan’s lungs are burning with heat;
if there is a matter, one must resolve it immediately. This year, the ninth month is already humid; next year, the spring air will come early. [He touched his head.]
The gate has three eyes; it must always be bright and clear. Watch over the water-buffalo of Mount Wei, lest it eat another’s grass.
When a fellow practitioner entered the mountain, he ascended the hall and said: "Jiaoshan lies secluded by the edge of the sea gates; to reach its midst requires past-life merit."
The Condition. One must encounter and realize this single phrase: "The spring breeze remains as it was in years past. This matter is like the spring breeze:
it pervades the entire Dharma-realm and arises according to the ground. When it passes through a sandalwood grove, the breeze is necessarily fragrant;
when it passes through a stall of fermented fish, the breeze is necessarily foul. Yet, the foulness has never truly been foul, nor has the fragrance ever truly been fragrant. Why is this so?

The nature of wind is fundamentally without fragrance or stench. That all sentient beings perceive its gathering and dispersing, perceive joy and sorrow, perceive coming and going, and perceive birth and death—all this is delusion.
If one understands it thus clearly, it may be said that "everywhere is true."
"Dust mote by dust mote, all are the person of original nature. Do you understand? Within the robe there is treasure year after year;
lacking the sinews in one's eyes, one is poor life after life.
Entering the hall, he said: "The spring colors have no high or low; the spring thunder is a sound that shakes the earth. A night of rain overturns the sky, dripping through—"
The Mind of the Patriarchs. A monk asked Master Guishan, "Today the rain is fine.
Guishan said, "Where is it fine? The monk had no reply. Guishan said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "Where is it fine? Guishan pointed to the rain. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "To advance from the top of a hundred-foot pole, one must be Guishan; coming and going in the rain, after all..."
He has never moistened his nostrils. Since he travels back and forth through the rain, why are his nostrils not wet?
It is simply because not even a single drop can enter them.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Jiaoshan has no leopard; he simply urges people to desist. Sentient beings are so deeply inverted that they poke through fire to seek bubbles.
Shigong mounted his bow and arrows; Juzhi raised his finger. If you can rest directly right now, it will all be like a bowl slipping from one's hand."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of the Chan practitioner Xian Daozhe, who traveled across the seas. One day he cried out, "What joy! What joy! A monk asked, "Master, you have such joy.
Xian said, "The wheat has ripened and been harvested before the mountain; let us not let the cowherd boy go in vain.
"Today at Jiaoshan," [the Master] said, "it is even more joyful than that of Xian Daozhe. Suppose someone were to ask me suddenly: 'I do not know, how is it?'"
"How pleasant! I simply said to him: 'In the kitchen there are people cooking rice; in the hall there are people discussing Zen.
It is well for the Elder of Jiaoshan to simply sleep crosswise or upright.'"

Last night, the void performed a somersault, startling the blue-eyed barbarian from the West.
